Item and finding shapes are documented in loop/README.md. `tiers` is a PROJECT-CONFIGURABLE list, not a fixed taxonomy — add or rename tiers to match this project's dependency graph, and keep `current_tier` pointing at one of them. items.decision_log: Maker: --color-<leaf> naming, unprefixed, deliberately colliding with 10 OSUI :root names because that IS the re-branding mechanism (149 consumers of var(--color-primary)); ramps preserved non-uniform; accent-cool and info both emitted at #00BDE3, not aliased; no white/black invented. Checker: core depth, 52/52 measured twice by two methods across 2 viewports, cascade provenance verified, framework consequences settled by measuring rendered widgets rather than reading declarations — which is what surfaced FND-001. Round 2 corrected a comment that inferred consumption from naming.

Nine-step size ramp, design step names preserved (3xs..3xl), sparse USWDS scale indices left uninterpolated, px kept as the design states with the rem trade-off declared not taken silently. Round 1 built 42px for 2xl because the REF said 42px; the checker measured glyph ink in the exported render, flagged it as a 5.4% outlier against a k=5.51 fit, and returned BLOCKED rather than FAIL because the defect was in the ref, not the build. get_design_context on the sample node confirmed 40px. Ref re-frozen from per-node text styles; the discredited layer-name sourcing is recorded in spec.md so it is not repeated.

items.visual: n/a — token-only item, no rendered surface of its own
items.decision_log: Family/weight/line-height only; sizes left to tok-font-sizes, which already owns them in the same file. Six of eight Prose steps are bound Figma variables; h3 and h6 are bound to nothing and were read from the sample nodes' own text styles via get_design_context (12:115, 12:119) rather than from layer names — the sourcing error tok-font-sizes made in round 1. Emitted Public Sans (the ref names a face, so the TODO the font-sizes ref could not close is closed here), weights 400/700 only, and three line-heights 1.62/1.2/1.15. Dropped the template's --font-weight-medium: 500: nothing on the node uses 500, and its only in-repo consumer carries an explicit fallback. Measured the framework rather than assuming: OSUI names weights --font-light/regular/semi-bold/bold (300/400/600/700), NOT --font-weight-*, so these names re-brand nothing on their own; and OSUI hard-codes its font stack in the html rule instead of reading a variable, so --font-family-base has no framework consumer either. Re-pointing --font-semi-bold (33 consumers, no 600 in this design) is the change that would actually re-brand widgets — deliberately left to the override layer, since this ref says nothing about OutSystems widgets. Kept --line-height-base as the name for the body value to avoid breaking its no-fallback consumer in the palette specimen. Two findings raised, none normalised: FND-008 (h3/h6 Regular where every other heading is Bold — and they are exactly the two unbound steps), FND-009 (Link/link-visited #562B97 has no palette entry). Independent corroboration of FND-005: this node states h1 = 40px, confirming the round-2 correction of the 2xl step from the mislabelled 42px.

items.visual: pass (colour + geometry); button WIDTH unverified — Public Sans is not hosted, so the preview renders the fallback face
items.decision_log: Restyled the native .btn rather than building a parallel system. Colour is carried by --uswds-button-* custom properties set on .btn and reassigned per variant, so 44 states cost ~20 flat rules instead of 38 specificity arguments. Geometry: the ref reports the SAME 93x38 box for filled and outline despite a 2px stroke, so the Figma stroke is inside-aligned; padding is therefore 10/18 (ref 12/20 less the border) with a 2px border transparent on filled variants, which reproduces 38.4 and 93 exactly and keeps filled/outline interchangeable without a 4px layout shift. Neutralised two framework mechanisms that would have silently defeated the ref: OSUI expresses hover/active as filter:brightness(), which would have multiplied the ref hover colour (killed at matching 0,3,0 and VERIFIED by injecting .desktop, since the preview harness sets no device class); and OSUI re-pins button heights on .tablet/.phone at 0,2,0. Bare .btn maps to the ref outline type, so a Button with no Style lands on a correct USWDS button. Three judgments recorded in the handover for review: shared disabled appearance for the six variants the ref never draws (user decision, 2026-08-26); .btn-cancel MAPPED to the ref base type because the base rule would otherwise have left it primary-blue; .btn-small restored to framework geometry rather than inventing a small USWDS size. Two mistakes caught by measuring rather than by reading: the custom-property indirection alone left every disabled button on OSUI #ADB5BD because OSUI .btn[disabled] sets color/border as REAL properties at 0,2,0 over .btn at 0,1,0 — real properties restated at matching specificity; and .btn-small silently collapsed into the regular size because the base font-size won on source order. Findings: FND-010 filed as issue #15 (accent-warm 2.24:1 at rest, high) and FND-011 register-only (accent-cool hover 3.01:1, medium) — both built as designed, neither repaired. FND-001 .btn-success half closed BY THE DESIGN: the ref binds ink on success (5.49:1), so it lands under fidelity rather than as a contrast fix; the .alert-* half stays open for cmp-alert. Focus ring added without a finding per CLAUDE.md, in the ref own ink (white on the two inverse variants). Adds --color-white to tokens/colors.css: the palette ref contained no white and correctly invented none, and this ref binds Base/white as the foreground of 19 of 38 states, so the blank is filled by evidence rather than by default.

Generated from tokens/colors.css rather than hand-written, because the harness rule keeps preview chrome token-only and class-only; a hand-maintained specimen drifts from the palette and a drifted specimen shows a colour the build no longer emits. Hex is text content, never a CSS value, so a chip disagreeing with its own label is visible. Generator exits non-zero on a token matching no ramp rather than silently omitting it.

Reconciled into state 2026-08-26, after the fact: shipped in PR #11 (release v0.2.0 + typography specimen) and corrected in PR #13 (use the real widget per piece of content, not styled Containers). It was built and merged without ever having a row here, which is the gap this entry closes.

Font sizes page labels the 2xl row 42px but styles its sample 40px. Built as 40px. Below the high+ gate, so register-only.

--font-size-xs collides with OSUI 12px across 26 consumers; zero rendered defect measured. Mapping question for the semantic/overrides layer: OSUI xs is its smallest-text role and 3xs 13px is closer than the 15px that lands there by name.
